findings.title: GitHub Actions checked out via floating major tag, not commit SHA
findings.evidence: auto-tag.yml:46, ci.yml:18, release.yml:47 all use "uses: actions/checkout@v7" (a mutable major-version tag GitHub can repoint), while the same release.yml already pins softprops/action-gh-release to a commit SHA with a version comment (line 197). auto-tag.yml and release.yml run with top-level "permissions: contents: write" (push to main, create tags, create releases), so any step in those jobs, including checkout, executes with push/release privileges.
findings.impact: actions/checkout is first-party and tag-protected by GitHub, so realistic exploit probability is low, but the pin is inconsistent with the SHA-pinning already applied to the one third-party action in this repo, and it runs inside the two privileged (contents: write) workflows.
findings.fix: Pin actions/checkout to a commit SHA (currently tag v7.0.1) with a version comment, matching the convention already used for softprops/action-gh-release, at least in auto-tag.yml and release.yml.
findings.test_red_green: No automated test possible for a CI pin; verify manually that a workflow run still checks out the correct commit after repinning (compare the resolved SHA to the tag before merging).
findings.cetico_evidence: actions/checkout@v7 at ci.yml:18, release.yml:47 and auto-tag.yml:46. release.yml:197 pins softprops by SHA. It runs under contents: write (auto-tag.yml:24-25, release.yml:27-28). First-party action, so the risk is low.

findings.title: ci.yml has no explicit permissions block (relies on repo/org default token scope)
findings.evidence: ci.yml declares no top-level or job-level permissions key, unlike auto-tag.yml (line 25: contents: write) and release.yml (line 28: contents: write) which both scope explicitly. ci.yml only builds/tests and never pushes or creates releases.
findings.impact: Token scope for this workflow is implicit and depends on the repository/organization default (Settings > Actions > Workflow permissions), which can be changed independently of this file. If that default is ever set to read-and-write, every future step added to ci.yml silently inherits write access it does not need.
findings.fix: Add an explicit least-privilege permissions block to ci.yml, e.g. permissions: contents: read at the workflow level.
findings.test_red_green: No red/green test applies; verify by re-running the workflow and confirming it still passes with contents: read (it makes no writes today).
findings.cetico_evidence: ci.yml has no permissions key (grep finds none). auto-tag.yml:24 and release.yml:27 do declare one. The category 'abandoned' is mislabeled.

findings.title: select-swift action has no upper bound: always builds with the newest Xcode on the runner image
findings.evidence: action.yml:42 does find /Applications -maxdepth 1 -name Xcode*.app | sort -V | tail -1 and only enforces a floor (>= 6.2, action.yml:64-71); there is no ceiling or pin to a specific tested Xcode/Swift version. ci.yml and release.yml both run on the fixed label macos-15 (ci.yml:16, release.yml:43), but the preinstalled Xcode versions on that label are updated by GitHub over time, independent of this repo.
findings.impact: The action own comment (action.yml:6-17) documents that a version mismatch between ci.yml and release.yml already caused a green main and a broken release once. The current floor-only design reproduces the same class of risk from a different direction: a runner-image update that adds a newer major Xcode would silently change the compiler both workflows build with, with no corresponding commit in this repo and no warning, since the check only fails on versions that are too old, never on ones that are untested and newer.
findings.fix: Either pin to a specific Xcode version present on macos-15 that matches what the maintainer validates locally, or add an explicit upper-bound/allow-list check that fails loudly (like the existing floor check) when the newest available Xcode exceeds the last version this package was verified against.
findings.package: select-swift (local composite action) / macos-15 runner image
findings.test_red_green: Not expressible as a code test; process check: on the next macos-15 image bump, confirm CI reports the same Swift version scripts/with-test-toolchain.sh selects locally before merging.
findings.cetico_evidence: action.yml:42 picks the newest Xcode and only enforces a floor (:64-71). Downgraded: ci and release share the action, so they no longer drift from each other (the documented failure mode), and shipped DMGs are built locally, not in CI (CLAUDE.md Releasing). A newer Xcode can only turn CI red visibly; it cannot silently change a shipped binary.
